wrong.name: Nordstrand bad
wrong.why: The only beach Norway ships (tier 2, rank 1, and the index top_beach). It is an urban bathing establishment in Oslo on the Indre Oslofjord, built around 1890 for patients of the Fageraas sanatorium and later extended with a restaurant, theatre hall, concert hall and bowling alley. It is a municipal badeplass in a residential Oslo suburb, not a beach a traveller would cross the country for, and it is the wrong single object to represent Norwegian beaches. Its record carries sources ['osm'] only and no bathing water class, unlike every SE/FI/DK beach.

missing.name: Hauklandstranda (Haukland Beach)
missing.why: Lofoten's flagship white sand beach, Blue Flag certified, named by Visit Norway among Europe's most beautiful. Wikidata classes it as a beach (P31 Q40080) but stores no coordinate, so the lat/lon here come from the OSM natural=beach way named Hauklandstranda, Vestvagoy.

missing.name: Uttakleivstranda (Uttakleiv Beach)
missing.why: The beach next to Haukland on Vestvagoy, listed by Visit Norway as one of the beaches that draw visitors to Lofoten. No Wikidata item found for the beach itself; coordinates are the OSM natural=beach way named Uttakleivstranda, so it is marked unverified.

missing.name: Kvalvika
missing.why: Bay on Moskenesoya, Lofoten, whose beach is one of Norway's best known hike-in beaches (from Fredvang). Wikidata item is the bay (P31 Q39594) with a coordinate.

missing.name: Bunes Beach (Bunesstranda)
missing.why: Beach on Moskenesoya reached by ferry to Vindstad and a walk over the pass; named by Visit Norway alongside Haukland and Ramberg as a Lofoten beach draw. Wikidata P31 Q40080 beach in Norway.

missing.name: Solastranden
missing.why: Two kilometre sand beach on Jaeren, minutes from Stavanger airport, the busiest bathing beach of southwest Norway and an obvious pick for a country whose beach tab is otherwise empty.

missing.name: Refviksanden
missing.why: Wide white sand beach on Vagsoy in Nordfjord, Wikidata P31 Q40080 beach in Vagsoy, Norway. Sits close to the Hoddevik catalogue destination that already exists in the app.

missing.name: Sjosanden
missing.why: Mandal's 800 metre sand beach, the best known bathing beach of southern Norway.

missing.name: Ersfjordstranda
missing.why: Senja's signature beach with the National Tourist Route facilities. No Wikidata item found; the coordinate is the OSM object named Ersfjordstranda at Ersfjorden, Senja, so it is marked unverified.

missing.name: Orrestranda
missing.why: The longest sand beach on Jaeren and part of the Jaeren protected landscape. A Wikidata item exists and is placed in Norway (P17 Q20) but it carries no coordinate and no usable label, so coordinates are left null rather than guessed.

order: There is no ranking to defend: the country ships exactly one beach, in tier 2, and it is an Oslo bathing establishment.

Root cause is visible in the data. SE/FI/DK beach rows carry sources ['eea','osm'] and an EEA bathing water class (27/32, 32/34, 46/49 rows). Norway's single row carries sources ['osm'] and no water class, so the beach candidate pool is effectively the EEA bathing water join, which returns nothing for Norway. Until an OSM natural=beach plus Wikidata P31=Q40080 path is added, Norway will keep shipping an empty Beaches tab.

Hoddevik already exists as a catalogue destination (gem:hoddevik) and is a surf beach, yet no beach was harvested there. Same for Lofoten, where five Blue Flag or nationally famous beaches lie within 20 km of each other.

wrong.name: Kjeragbolten
wrong.why: Tier 1, rank 4, ranked one place above Kjerag itself at rank 5, 1.2 km away. Kjeragbolten is a boulder wedged in a crevice on the Kjerag massif, not a separate mountain. One mountain is occupying two of Norway's twelve tier 1 slots.

wrong.name: Vestkapp
wrong.why: Tier 2, rank 19. Vestkapp (Kjerringa) on Stadlandet is a coastal cape and plateau viewpoint reached by road, not a summit. It belongs on a viewpoints layer, not in a mountains ranking.

wrong.name: Sverd i fjell
wrong.why: Tier 2, rank 77. A 1983 bronze monument of three swords driven into rock at Hafrsfjord, Stavanger. It is a sculpture, not a mountain; it entered the mountain list because its name contains fjell.

missing.name: Galdhopiggen
missing.why: At 2469 m the highest mountain in Norway and in Northern Europe, and a guided summer walk-up from Juvasshytta. A Norwegian mountains tab without it is not credible. Jotunheimen is represented only by Glittertinden (rank 9) and a string of unnamed Hellstugu and Memuru tops.

missing.name: Trolltunga
missing.why: The single most photographed hike in Norway, above Ringedalsvatnet at Odda. Wikidata classes it as a rock formation (P31 Q1404150), the same category as Preikestolen and Kjeragbolten which the tab already carries, so the tab's own scope demands it.

missing.name: Besseggen
missing.why: The most walked mountain ridge in Norway (Jotunheimen, boat from Gjendesheim), around 30,000 walkers a season, and completely absent while four unnamed Geiranger tops sit in tier 1.

missing.name: Snohetta
missing.why: 2286 m, the highest peak of Dovrefjell and the mountain of the Dovrefjell-Sunndalsfjella national park and the Snohetta viewpoint pavilion.

missing.name: Stetind
missing.why: 1392 m granite obelisk in Narvik municipality, voted Norway's national mountain in a 2002 national poll.

missing.name: Segla
missing.why: The sail shaped peak above Fjordgard on Senja, one of the most photographed mountains in northern Norway. Northern Norway is represented in tier 1 by nothing at all.

missing.name: Reinebringen
missing.why: The Lofoten viewpoint over Reine, rebuilt with 1566 Sherpa stone steps and now one of the busiest short hikes in Norway.

missing.name: Romsdalseggen
missing.why: The ridge walk above Andalsnes, the standard companion to Trollstigen, which is already a catalogue destination (gem:trollstigen) represented only by Store Trolltinden and Romsdalshornet.

missing.name: Store Skagastolstind (Storen)
missing.why: 2405 m, Norway's third highest and the country's most storied climbing peak in Hurrungane, Jotunheimen.

missing.name: Skala
missing.why: 1848 m above Loen in Nordfjord with the Skalatarnet stone tower, one of the classic long ascents in Western Norway and adjacent to the Loen Skylift.

order: Geographic clustering dominates tier 1. Seven of twelve tier 1 mountains sit within 8 km of Geiranger (Dalsnibba, Blahornet, Eidshornet, Saetertverrfjellet, Holedalsfjellet, plus Djupdalsegga and Steegga just below in tier 2). Blahornet, Eidshornet and Saetertverrfjellet all score exactly 0.980, which is the signature of a flag, not of fame.

The flag is UNESCO: 21 of the 116 Norwegian mountains carry sources ['osm','whc'] and they are exactly the Geirangerfjord tops. A world heritage polygon should not lift every knoll inside it above Galdhopiggen, Besseggen and Trolltunga, which are absent entirely.
Kjeragbolten (rank 4) above Kjerag (rank 5) is backwards and duplicated.
Floyen (rank 11) and Ulriken (rank 12), the two Bergen funicular and cable car hills, are defensible as attractions but not above the ten missing entries listed here.
Dalsnibba at rank 1 is a road accessible viewpoint at 1476 m. It is a fine top ten entry; it is not the mountain of Norway.

counts_verdict: 1 beach and 116 mountains is wrong on both sides. One beach for a country with roughly 100,000 km of coastline, Blue Flag beaches in Lofoten and Jaeren, and a surf destination already in the catalogue is a pipeline failure, not a reflection of Norway. 116 mountains is a reasonable raw pool, but tier 1 holding only 12 with 7 from one fjord is over-concentrated; a country this size should show 12 tier 1 mountains drawn from at least 8 different regions.
top_pick_verdict: Both picks fail. top_beach 'Nordstrand bad' is an Oslo bathing establishment illustrated with a 1910 photograph; a Norway beach card should show Hauklandstranda or Uttakleivstranda in Lofoten. top_mountain 'Dalsnibba' is a road viewpoint; the country card should be Galdhopiggen (highest), Preikestolen (most recognisable) or Trolltunga.
notes: Provenance tells the story: every beach in SE/FI/DK carries 'eea' in sources, Norway's single beach does not, so the beach layer is EEA-bound and Norway contributes no rows to that register. Second, the tab mixes summits with cliffs and rock formations (Preikestolen, Kjeragbolten) and with a monument (Sverd i fjell) and a rock arch (Kirkeporten, tier 2 rank 57 at Skarsvag); if the tab is 'mountains and viewpoints' that should be explicit, and monuments and entrenchments (Korthaugen Entrenchment, tier 2 rank 106) should still be filtered out. Third, elevation_m is null on every Norwegian feature, which removes the one signal that would have ranked Galdhopiggen and Glittertinden above a 400 m Bergen hill.
